title: The Secret of the King's Letters
synopsis: A paper in the King's new letters is half burnt.
Four little groups are lost. Only the night guard saw them.
goal: Find the four groups and what they mean, before the rain.

options.label: The scholars' hall: 혼
options.feedback: Scholars write Chinese characters well. And Taek saw the dot below the line.

options.label: The guard post: 운
options.feedback: No bucket stands here. And Taek saw 2 short lines on top.

options.label: The path to the kitchen well: 훈

notes: Picture gate_courtyard (2026-11-04): the scholars' hall doorway (left), the guard post with its brazier (right middle) and the path to the kitchen well with its jars (far right) are drawn in it and measured on this file (grid sheet). The three traces lie on the plain paving in front of the steps.

Traces read (DeductionScene): 門 copied from the gate sign (the writer could not write Chinese characters), a bucket ring and water drops all point to the path to the kitchen well. Each place's chip shows the group drawn there; Taek's shape words pick the same one (훈: not 혼, its dot on top; not 운, no lines on top).
The three traces are drawn by the app over their areas (copiedScrap, waterRing, waterDrops): no writing is ever in a picture.

2026-11-06: each trace is reached through a second, larger area (its first area is where the app draws it); the tap guide stands just under the copied scrap, on bare paving in the marks' row (never on a trace: it shows how to look, not where).

2026-11-06: the opening view is the row of marks with the guard post and the kitchen well path (x 520–1536, y 700–920): the picture opens about 1.5× larger on a phone; the scholars' hall is a swipe to the left. The drops are a longer trail (1000–1420), curving past the guard post into the well path.

2026-11-07: the groups are the options' words (chips): none is drawn in the picture. 훈's meaning is never said: the talk after says it is what Sora does for Bun-i, and Sora teaches her; Final B asks for it (TEACH, not LEARN).

learning.objective: 세종의 말과 흔적 문장, 택의 모양 설명을 읽고 글쓴이가 어디서 왔는지, 어떤 글자가 그 사람의 것인지 추리한다.
expressions: Many people cannot write what they want to say.

play.title: The Paper Under the Gate
story: Who left it at the gate?
play.letter:
The King said: "Many people cannot write what they want to say."
Someone copied 門 from the gate sign, three times.
A wet ring: a water bucket stood here.
Drops of water lead away from the gate, past the guard post.
Sora's 3 pupils each drew one group in charcoal by their place.
Taek saw a ring with 2 short lines on top. Under it: a flat line, a dot below it, then a corner.
play.question: Which place has the writer's group? Tap the place.
hints: Tap the paper scrap, the wet ring and the drops of water.
Who carries water? Then read Taek's shapes again.
play.successMessage: The writer carries water from the kitchen well!
transition: At the well, the water-carriers know the hand at once.
"That is Bun-i's group," says one. "She went home at sunset."
"She says it is what Sora does for her every night."
"Sora, the palace maid, teaches her the new letters."

talk.speaker: taek
talk.goal: Find out where Taek found the paper.

lines.text: It was under the inner gate after sunset.
It had four little groups. I know the shapes, not the order.
Then we can build them again.

clue.title: The First Group
clue.note: Bun-i's group: what Sora does for her. Bun-i carries water. She could not write Chinese characters.

evidence.name: The Copied Scrap
evidence.description: 門 copied three times from the gate sign. The writer could not write Chinese characters.

traces.task: Tap 3 marks on the ground. Then tap a place.
traces.chooseTask: 3 marks found! Now tap the writer's place.
traces.missLine: Nothing here. Look on the ground.
traces.notPlaceLine: Tap a place the writer could have come from.

notes: Taek names the group by the body part Sora's board gives it, and its line: the board's English decides each letter, a Korean reader's eye alone does not.
Six tiles are not in the group: ㅂ answers 'no added line' (the board's rule, ㅁ + 1 line = ㅂ), ㅗ 'no dot', ㅣ 'flat', ㅅ ㄴ ㄱ a misread body part.
Letters are tiles of the app (text): never in a picture.

clueInputs.note: Bun-i wrote the paper; Sora teaches her.

learning.objective: 택이 말한 발음 기관(the throat, the mouth)과 선(a flat line), 획 규칙(no added line)을 소라의 판에 맞춰 방해 글자 사이에서 세 글자를 순서대로 고르고, 목구멍과 입이 만드는 '소리'의 글자임을 안다.
expressions: A stronger sound adds one line.

play.title: Sora's Lesson Box
story: Sora comes to the well with a lamp.
"Bun-i learned the new letters in ten days," she says.
"My pupils lock their slates in my lesson box."
Sora reads her board. Taek remembers the marks he saw.
play.letterIntro: Sora's lesson board, and Taek's memory:
play.letter:
SORA'S BOARD
These letters copy shapes:
ㄱ = the back of the tongue
ㄴ = the tongue on the gums
ㅁ = the mouth
ㅅ = the teeth
ㅇ = the throat
A flat line = the earth.
A stronger sound adds one line.
ㄴ + 1 line = ㄷ
ㄴ + 2 lines = ㅌ
ㅁ + 1 line = ㅂ

TAEK REMEMBERS
1. The throat.
2. A flat line, no dot.
3. The mouth at the bottom. No added line.
play.question: Which 3 letters open the box? Tap them in Taek's order.
hints: Find the throat and the mouth on Sora's board.
Read Taek's last line again: is a line added?
play.orderFeedback: Those are the right letters. Read Taek's lines in order.

feedback.ieung,i,mieum: The line is flat, not standing.
feedback.siot,eu,mieum: Line 1 is the throat, not the teeth.
feedback.nieun,eu,mieum: Line 1 is the throat, not the tongue.

transition: Inside is Bun-i's slate. It shows one group: 음.
"The throat and the mouth," says Sora. "This group means sound."
"She used one more paper in my writing room."

talk.speaker: sora
talk.goal: Find out how Bun-i learned to write.

lines.text: The King asked me: can people learn his letters in ten days?
Bun-i could not write one Chinese character. Today was her tenth day.
Her last test: write the name of the King's letters.
Then the marks Taek saw are her letters.

clue.title: The Second Group
clue.note: 음 = SOUND. The throat, a flat line, the mouth.

evidence.name: Sora's Lesson Board
evidence.description: The first letters copy the tongue, the mouth, the teeth and the throat. A stronger sound adds a line.

notes: Group 1 is built from Sora's words: ㅈ (the teeth + 1 line), ㅓ (dot left of a standing line), ㅇ at the bottom. Group 2 has no words of its own: it is the group of Bun-i's slate, the clue of Mission 2.
The two groups sit one above the other on Bun-i's paper (the board's TOP and BOTTOM). No writing rule is claimed for 1446.
Every letter is the app's text (SyllableBoard): never in a picture.

clueInputs.note: Group 2 is the group on Bun-i's slate.

learning.objective: 점(하늘)·누운 줄(땅)·선 줄(사람)과 위치 표현(on its left, at the bottom, at the top)을 읽어 첫 묶음을 만들고, 둘째 묶음은 앞 미션의 단서로 채운 뒤, '바른 소리'의 뜻을 안다.
expressions: a standing line, a dot on its left

play.title: Bun-i's Last Paper
story: You go to Sora's writing room.
"Dot = sky. Flat line = earth. Standing line = person."
play.letter:
Flat vowels go under.
Standing vowels go on the right.
Bun-i's 2 groups sit one above the other.
Group 1 is at the top.
play.question: Tap TOP or BOTTOM. Then choose FIRST SOUND, LINE, DOT and AT THE BOTTOM.
hints: Group 2 is in your notebook. Read your clue from the well.
Group 1: add one line to the teeth, not two.

feedback.장음: Group 1's dot is on the left of its line, not the right.
feedback.정응: Group 2 is not right. Read your clue from the well.

play.successMessage: The paper is whole again. Sora reads it out: "the right sounds"!
transition: "You know one group: sound. So this one means right."
"That is three groups," says Sora. "One is still lost."
"The King is at the book hall." The first drops of rain fall.

lines.text: Each group had lines and dots.
This paper had two groups, one above the other.

clue.title: The Third Group
clue.note: 정음 = the right sounds. 음 is sound, so 정 is right.

evidence.name: Bun-i's Note
evidence.description: Bun-i's note, put back together from Taek's memory. Two of its groups say: the right sounds.

blocks.line: Group 1 (TOP): the teeth + 1 line. A standing line, a dot on its left. AT THE BOTTOM: the throat.
Group 2 (BOTTOM): the group on Bun-i's slate.

notes: Stage A: King Sejong's three questions, shown evidence in turn (play.talk.before): the last says who the letters are for, the people. Stage B: this puzzle, on the final's page.

The groups already found are tiles of their meanings: a player who knows the name must still read the clues (TEACH, not LEARN: what Sora does for Bun-i). The fourth is a group: Taek's shape words choose 민 among 문 만 빈.
Every letter is the app's text: never in a picture. His words are made up (dossier fiction).

clueInputs.note: What Sora does for Bun-i: she teaches her.

learning.objective: 세종의 질문을 증거로 답해 새 글자가 누구를 위한 것인지 밝히고, 단서의 뜻과 영어 질문(What does the King want to do? Who is it for?)을 읽어 이름을 완성한다.

play.title: The King's Letters
story: Rain is falling. Servants hold cloth over the book hall.
King Sejong is there, watching over his new books.
"A paper in my letters?" he asks. "Show me."
play.letter:
Taek remembers the last group:
The mouth. A standing line, no dot.
The tongue on the gums at the bottom.

The name reads like this:
1. What does the King want to do?
2. Who is it for?
3 and 4. What does he give them? (Bun-i's note: the right sounds.)
play.question: Build the name: tap 4 tiles in order.
hints: Read your first clue. What does Sora do for Bun-i?
The last group: find the mouth, then a standing line.
transition: 훈민정음 (訓民正音): the name of the King's letters.
"The right sounds, to teach the people," says the King.
"You learned my letters in one night," says the King. "And Bun-i spoke to me with them."

ending.text: The tiles turn over, one by one: 훈민정음 (訓民正音).
At dawn, Bun-i comes back with her water bucket.

ending.speaker: bun_i
ending.text: The King read my letter? My very first letter?

ending.speaker: sora
ending.text: He did. And he says thank you.
Bun-i writes the four groups again on the burnt paper.

objectives: Find out who wrote the paper.
Build the name with the King.
intro: Autumn, 1446. You visit King Sejong in Hanyang.
"Many people cannot write what they want to say."
"Can you read my letters by dawn?"
At the gate, Guard Taek burns a strange paper.
You pull it out of the fire. Rain is coming!
play.caseSummary: Bun-i wrote the name of the King's letters on her tenth day. The paper burnt, so you found its four groups. The name means the right sounds, to teach the people.

notes: Seoul Case 01, redesigned 2026-11-07 (docs/SEOUL_CASE01_REDESIGN_PLAN.md): the four groups of Hunminjeongeum, found in the order 훈, 음, 정, 민 and built by their meanings.

King Sejong appears and speaks: every word of his is made up (dossier fiction), two lines retell his preface (h9, h5). Bun-i, Sora and Taek are made up. The four groups were never lost in history: only Bun-i's paper is.
